Log-linear conductance model with spline terms

Source: R/radish_conductance_model.R
smooth_loglinear_conductance.Rd

Returns a function of class "terradish_conductance_model" that represents a log-linear conductance surface after expanding selected numeric covariates into spline basis columns. The result is an unpenalized regression spline with a fixed number of coefficients, fitted through the selected terradish measurement likelihood.

Usage

smooth_loglinear_conductance(
  formula,
  x,
  df = 4L,
  basis = c("ns", "bs"),
  degree = 3L,
  intercept = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula describing which spatial covariates drive conductance. Smooth terms are written as s(variable, df = 4) or s(variable, k = 4). Ordinary linear terms can be mixed with smooth terms, e.g. ~ forestcover + s(altitude, df = 4).

x

Data frame of spatial covariates extracted from a conductance_surface object (typically surface$x).

df

Default degrees of freedom for smooth terms that do not supply df or k.

basis

Default spline basis. "ns" uses ns natural splines; "bs" uses bs B-splines.

degree

B-spline polynomial degree used when basis = "bs".

intercept

Logical; include intercept columns within each spline basis? The default is FALSE, matching terradish's usual convention of omitting a global conductance intercept.

Value

A function of class "terradish_conductance_model" that accepts a numeric vector of conductance parameters theta and returns conductance values plus derivative functions used internally by the optimizer. Derivatives are with respect to the expanded basis columns.

Details

The model first expands all s() terms into basis columns and then applies the same positive log-link used by loglinear_conductance:

$$C_i = \exp(B_i \theta)$$

Each spline column is centered over the active graph cells. The fitted knots, boundary knots, degree, and column centers are retained and reused for plotting, focal-support prediction, and coarse warm starts. Centering changes the arbitrary conductance reference level but preserves the likelihood and fitted conductance coefficients. Uncertainty bands are relative to the landscape-mean spline contribution to log conductance.

where \(B_i\) is the row of the expanded spline/parametric design matrix for grid cell \(i\). The same conductance factory works with MLPE and Wishart measurement models.

Smoothing parameters are not estimated in this first implementation. The effective smoothness is controlled by fixed basis dimension through df or k; use small values for stable first-pass model comparison. AIC and AICc at nominal Wishart information can over-select flexible curves. Prefer spatial CV for selecting conductance terms, and examine sensitivity to nu before interpreting uncertainty. Tails beyond the sampled covariate range are poorly identified. A selected curve can describe how a process maps onto the graph without identifying an ecological response mechanism.

summary(fit)$spline_monotonicity describes each fitted smooth over the range at focal sites. It reports whether the curve is monotone, its direction, and the number of derivative sign changes. This is a shape diagnostic, not an uncertainty test.

Worked example

See vignette("v06-spline-conductance", package = "terradish") for fitted conductance curves, genetic-response plots, and model comparison.

See also

loglinear_conductance, gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance, conductance_surface, terradish

Other conductance models: gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance(), loglinear_conductance(), terradish_conductance_model_factory

Examples

x <- data.frame(altitude = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8),
                forestcover = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1))
model <- smooth_loglinear_conductance(~ forestcover + s(altitude, df = 3), x)
theta <- attr(model, "default")
fit <- model(theta)
fit$conductance
#> [1] 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
